paper_metadata.title: Identification of clinical characteristics and factors predicting favorable treatment outcomes in elderly patients with traumatic brain injury

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the source population, recruitment period, and inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, it is a retrospective single-center study, which inherently carries a risk of selection bias. The participation rate of eligible individuals is not explicitly stated, making it difficult to determine if the sample is truly representative of all elderly TBI patients in the region.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Clinical and radiological data from 493 patients with TBI who visited a single institute were retrospectively collected from January 2014 to December 2015.
items.reasoning: The source (single institute) and the general population (TBI patients) are defined.

items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: We included patients who were admitted to the hospital through ED visits within 24 h after head trauma and those who were diagnosed with TBI.
items.reasoning: While the entry point (ED) is clear, the retrospective nature and single-center setting may introduce referral bias not fully addressed.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Exclusion criteria were: 1) age younger than 15 years, 2) presence of subacute to chronic hemorrhage, 3) presence of diffuse axonal injury, 4) presence of skull fracture alone (excluding intracranial hemorrhage), and 5) loss to 6 month follow-up visits.
items.reasoning: The criteria are detailed and specific.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study excludes patients lost to follow-up at 6 months. While the final analyzed sample is described, the number of patients excluded due to loss to follow-up is not quantified, nor are their characteristics compared to those who completed the study. This creates a risk of attrition bias if those lost to follow-up had different outcomes.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (GCS, ISS, Pupillary reflex, pSDH) are standard clinical metrics in neurosurgery. They were measured at the time of ED arrival using established scales, ensuring consistency across the cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary outcome (GOS-E at 6 months) is a validated, standard tool for TBI prognosis. While the paper doesn't explicitly mention blinding of the GOS-E assessors to the baseline prognostic factors, the use of a structured scale at a fixed time point limits bias.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The outcome of the elderly patients was dichotomized into two groups: favorable (good recovery to moderate disability; GOS-E > 4) and unfavorable (severe disability to death; GOS-E <= 4).
items.reasoning: The outcome and its dichotomization are clearly defined.

items.evidence_snippet: GOS-E is a global scale of functional outcome that rates patient status into one of eight categories.
items.reasoning: GOS-E is the gold standard for TBI outcome measurement.
